edit.description: the report location both operations name, and the stdout scan that stands in for being told
the operations' docs on what the runner adds to a consumer's own run
the report cases, driven through the real reporter

summary: the vitest runner tells vitest where to write its JSON report and reads it there; the stdout scan for the report's first bytes goes
acceptance: both run operations name an output file the runner owns and read the report out of it, so a tool that writes its report somewhere other than stdout is still read; the refusal over a report claiming success against a non-zero exit survives the move
tests: the vitest runner reads its report from the file it told vitest to write
pins: a report claiming success over a non-zero exit is still refused
notes: `parseReport` searches stdout for the report's first bytes amid whatever plugins printed — the location inferred rather than told (`engine-boundary.md`, *Told, not inferred*), holding only while the tool keeps printing there. Consumer-measured: vitest 5's json reporter writes to a file by default and the runner then refuses "no JSON report". This repo pins vitest 2.1.9, so the case is the real reporter writing to the told path. Same modules as its blocker.
